title: Swift Flight Form: the raven’s legacy
summary: A Druid follows Morthis Whisperwing from Moonglade’s sleeping barrows to Outland’s raven cult. The recovered book names Anzu; three separate shrine trials and the Southfury Moonstone prepare the confrontation, while Morthis’s final warning leaves the future open.
opening: The marsh refuge offers a promise: Morthis can teach the Stormcrow’s secrets, if a Druid is willing to follow the evidence. What begins as a troubling dream leads through an old book, three guarded essences, and a stone that can call the Raven God into reach.

chapters.title: A warning within the Dream
chapters.body:
Among Zangarmarsh’s spore towers and shallow waters, Morthis Whisperwing offered a druid the secrets of the swift stormcrow form. His teaching began with a trial. Beyond the refuge waited knowledge that could not be gained by strength alone. In the drowned green country, a promise of flight opened a search into an older danger, carried through sleepers, spirits and scattered memory.

Morthis prepared a ward from the materials the seeker brought him. A sleeper waited in Moonglade’s barrows, and waking him would require care. The search for knowledge had acquired a responsibility to the one who kept it. Before the druid could hear what the dormant witness knew, the ward had to offer protection against the danger of his awakening.

Beneath Moonglade’s pines, the Stormrage Barrow Dens kept their old silence. In the southern den, Clintar Dreamwalker stirred beneath Morthis’s ward. He woke confused, carrying the burden of what he had witnessed. His spirit had to be followed beyond the waking world, where the divided soul could speak more freely than the body left behind.

Within a dream echo, Clintar’s spirit led the seeker toward three Relics of Aviana. Dreamwarden Lurosa helped keep the passage open. An Aspect of the Raven threatened the work. Clintar feared an outside presence, but that remained the witness’s suspicion. The relics were recovered from the dream, while the cause of its danger remained a question to carry back.

Morthis received the relics and Clintar’s warning. Neither could fully explain what had entered the Dream. If an older raven tradition held a clue, its history might still be found in Outland. He sent the seeker toward Arthorn Windsong in the Evergrove. The search turned from tending a sleeping guardian toward a memory that had outlasted its keepers.

chapters.title: The raven’s broken history
chapters.body:
The Evergrove offered green shelter among Blade’s Edge’s broken ridges. There Arthorn Windsong studied an old raven cult. Her work promised a lead without yet explaining Clintar’s fear. The druids needed to recover a history scattered and buried. Before a dangerous power could be confronted, the quiet grove became a place of study, drawing the search toward those who remembered its lost book.

Arthorn’s notes and Timeon’s clue led to Sai’kkal near the Vortex Pinnacle. A Seer’s Stone and an aether ray’s eye let the seeker perceive the arakkoa shade. Sai’kkal spoke of a raven book stolen, broken apart and buried. Its pieces lay at Skettis. The scattered words might name what troubled Clintar, if the lost work could be made whole enough to read.

From Blade’s Edge, the search turned toward Nagrand’s open grasslands. On Twilight Ridge, Watcher Elaira knew a way to seek what lay hidden. Beyond the spirit’s testimony waited buried fragments that the druid could not readily find. A living creature’s keen sight might reach them, carrying the search from broken memory toward the ground where its scattered words remained.

A wild sparrowhawk was trained to find the buried Raven Stones at Skettis. When its help was no longer needed, it would be released. For a time, the bird’s sight became an ally to the druids’ search. What memory and testimony had left incomplete could now be recovered from the earth, and the old book might yield the name they sought.

At Skettis, the Raven Stones were gathered and Arthorn reconstructed the book. Its words named Anzu as the Raven God and described three bird spirits bound to shrines. A name had emerged from the fragments, though the recovered prophecy still demanded care. The druid now faced separate trials in Terokkar, seeking the power needed to bring the dangerous being within reach.

chapters.title: Three essences of Terokkar
chapters.body:
At the first shrine, the Eagle guardian confronted the seeker. Its defeat yielded an essence to carry onward. The Bone Wastes held old places whose meanings had not vanished with their keepers. One spirit’s power had been gathered, but the preparation was incomplete. Two more shrines awaited the druid whose search had begun among the refuge’s green waters.

Beside Lake Ere’Noru, another shrine held the Falcon guardian. The seeker prevailed, and its essence joined the Eagle’s. Each spirit guarded its own place, each encounter adding to the preparation Arthorn had named. Beyond the lake remained Sorrow Wing Point. The Raven God had been identified, but the means to confront him still depended upon the last shrine’s challenge.

At Sorrow Wing Point, the Hawk guardian held the final shrine. Its defeat brought the third essence into the seeker’s hands. Eagle, Falcon and Hawk had each marked a separate trial. Together their powers could return to Cenarion Refuge, where Morthis would judge the preparation. The old book had supplied a name; the druid still needed a way to summon its bearer.

The essences returned to Cenarion Refuge with Arthorn’s report. Morthis warned that Anzu was powerful, and the trials had not yet made a direct summons possible. Another object had to be recovered. Knowledge and readiness had brought the druid this far, but the Raven God remained beyond reach until the means of calling him could be placed within the seeker’s hands.

chapters.title: A summons and an open threat
chapters.body:
In Azshara, the search for the Southfury Moonstone became a pursuit involving Rizzle Sprysprocket. The stone was recovered. Its purpose gave the final preparation a focus: the druids hoped to use it to summon Anzu. Open country now gave way to the halls of Auchindoun, where the object could bring the Raven God into the confrontation the old book had made possible.

Beneath Sethekk Halls’ broken arches, the Moonstone was placed in the Raven’s Claw. Anzu answered. The druid confronted and defeated him, gaining the swift stormcrow form Morthis had promised. The search had crossed dream and waking lands to reach this reckoning. Yet a victory over the Raven God could not promise that every danger to the Dream had ended.

At Cenarion Refuge, Morthis warned that Anzu’s followers might help him rise again. The Moonstone was kept for another day. The stormcrow’s knowledge had been won, and the Raven God defeated, but vigilance remained. Beyond the recovered book and the broken halls lay an unanswered future, entrusted to those who would remember the warning and keep watch.
